question.problem:
Given that ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{40}∼N(12,{20}^{2})$ is a random sample of size $40$ from a normal population, calculate $P(\overset{―}{X}<11).$

*Hint: A value table of $Φ(z)$ for different values of $z$ is given below, where $Φ(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution. *

| $z$ | $\,0.01\,$ | $\,0.02\,$ | $\,0.03\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,-0.3\,$ | $\,0.3783\,$ | $\,0.3745\,$ | $\,0.3707\,$ |
| $\,-0.2\,$ | $\,0.4168\,$ | $\,0.4129\,$ | $\,0.4090\,$ |
| $\,-0.1\,$ | $\,0.4562\,$ | $\,0.4522\,$ | $\,0.4483\,$ |
question.worked_solution:
If ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{n}$ is a random sample of size $n$ from a normal population, where 

$$
{X}_{i}∼N(\mu ,{\sigma }^{2}),\,1\le i\le n,
$$

then the sample mean $\overset{―}{X}$ has the distribution

$$
\overset{―}{X}∼N(\mu ,\frac{{\sigma }^{2}}{n}).
$$

Therefore, the distribution of the sample mean $\overset{―}{X}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{X} & ∼N\,(12,\frac{{20}^{2}}{40}) \\  & ∼N(12,10).\end{aligned}
$$

We're required to find $P(\overset{―}{X}<11).$

First, we transform $X$ into a standard normal random variable $Z$ by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(\overset{―}{X}<11) & =P(Z<\frac{11-12}{\sqrt{10}}) \\  & =P(Z<-0.32) \\  & =Φ(-0.32)\end{aligned}
$$

From the table, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}Φ(-0.32)=0.3745.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(\overset{―}{X}<11) & =Φ(-0.32) \\  & =0.3745.\end{aligned}
$$
